text: An ___ on an index set $I$ is a maximal filter; equivalently, for every subset $A \subseteq I$ either $A$ or its complement $I \setminus A$ belongs to it.
explanation: A maximal filter is an ultrafilter, characterized by the dichotomy that for each $A \subseteq I$ exactly one of $A$, $I \setminus A$ is a member, which is the property that drives Los's theorem. A plain filter (closed under supersets and finite intersections) need not have this maximality, and an ideal is the dual notion.
